chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: House bands at the Bell Tavern, Alabam and Shep's Playhouse
summary: Patsy and Collette recall house bands at Los Angeles clubs: C. L. Burke at the Bell Tavern, Johnny Otis at the Alabam, Shep's Playhouse.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And here, what other bands did you work with.
They were more or less housebands at these clubs.
At the Bell Tavern, was that C. L. Burke?
Yes, C.L. Burke was there, yes, C. L. Burke had the Bell Tavern.
What year was that, the Bell Tavern.
That was in the thirties, I think, I think '37 or '38, I believe, I am not sure.
What other house band?
In other words, they are musicians that they have formed. Not no well known name or anything.

One of our purposes for doing this, if you just get names of working musicians in Los Angeles, especially outstanding ones, because there is so little history of Los Angeles music, and so any bands that you remember as especially being very good, or any individual musicians, who were outstanding and maybe not recognized. We are interested in them.
I can't think right now, but there are a lot of musicians who have played in these little different places that are well known and outstanding as of today, but I can't recall any of the names.
What about the Club Alabam.
Yeah, Johnny Otis' band was there, yeah.
What about Joe Wilson, was he there at the time.
Was Joe Wilson there. He might have been, I can't recall, but I know Johnny Otis.
What about this place that used to be down on First Street, there used to be a club downstairs.
Shep's Playhouse.
Yeah, it was Shep's.
That wasn't on First Street, that
was on Fourth or Fifth, Fifth or Sixth, or something like that. It was on sixth.
Did they have a show there that you know of.
I think so. That was during the time -- it was in the forties because it was during the time of the war.
-- broadcasting up in Oakland.
But I don't know what orchestra or band was there at the time.
We played at the Alabam with Cee Pee Johnson.
Yes, Cee fee was there. Buddy Banks and --
(inaudible)

At one time I think Buck Clayton. Yeah, Red Mack. I believe Buck Clayton worked there, but I can't think who he worked with. No, he didn't have his own, he was working with someone at the Club Alabam, and I can't recall who it was.
